clock.semantics: Integer day relative to the transfer. The article gives no calendar dates. Day 18 is the follow-up marrow (outcome only). day = null means the fact is valid at any point in the admission.

vignette: A 56-year-old woman is transferred from another hospital with severe pancytopenia; the referring team was concerned about aplastic anaemia. She received one unit of red cells before transfer and is on intravenous antimicrobials for presumed colitis and mucositis.
opening_statement_lay: I've been so tired and weak for weeks, and I get out of breath just walking around the house. The other hospital said my blood counts were very low and sent me here.

facts.release_text: Hypothyroidism after a total thyroidectomy some years ago. The referring team also records malnutrition.

facts.item: Previous operations (hidden until the surgical history is taken)
facts.release_text: Total thyroidectomy some years ago, and a sleeve gastrectomy.

release_condition.note: The article lists the gastric sleeve in the past history. The transfer letter (H04) and the medical history (H02) do not name it, so a player must take the surgical history (or find the port-site scars or ask about admissions).

facts.release_text: Transferred from another hospital with severe pancytopenia; the referring team was concerned about aplastic anaemia.
At the referring hospital she received one unit of packed red cells before transfer and was started on intravenous cefepime, metronidazole and fluconazole for presumed colitis and mucositis.
Physical examination on arrival recorded as unremarkable.

single_results.note: Printed 7.7 g/dL (normal 12.6-15.9 g/dL). After one unit of packed red cells at the referring hospital.
Printed 92.2 fL. Normocytic despite the deficiency; the authors cite the transfusion, hypothyroidism, protein malnutrition and the later pneumonia.
Printed '< 6 k/L' (normal 159-439 k/uL); read as <6 x10^9/L, an obvious misprint of k/uL.
Printed absolute neutrophil count 0.06 k/uL; no reference range printed, catalogue range used.

Printed 2.6 pg/mL (normal >=5.9 pg/mL); pg/mL is a misprint for ng/mL, so 2.6 ng/mL = 5.9 nmol/L and the limit 5.9 ng/mL = 13.4 nmol/L. Reported one day after the marrow; placed on day 0 as sent with the admission bloods (method decision, turnaround applies in play).
Tested by FISH on the marrow in the article; the catalogue's BCR-ABL1 test is recorded with the same result.

raw_material.findings: Red cells with minimal anisopoikilocytosis. Eosinophils increased (50% of leucocytes) with frequent atypical nuclear segmentation. Rare hypogranular neutrophils.
Eosinophils increased (54% of viable leucocytes); myeloid blasts slightly increased (1.5% of viable leucocytes); no abnormal B-cell, T-cell, NK-cell or mast cell populations.

Erythroid-predominant trilineage haematopoiesis; 12% blasts and 15% eosinophils by morphology; dyserythropoiesis and dysmegakaryopoiesis. Erythroid maturation left-shifted with increased pronormoblasts and basophilic normoblasts; frequent erythroid precursors with megaloblastic changes, cytoplasmic vacuolisation, nuclear contour irregularities, nuclear budding, macronuclei and multinucleation. Frequent small hypolobate megakaryocytes, megakaryocytes with hyperlobate nuclei and with widely spaced nuclear lobes. Granulocytes with a prominent left shift; blasts with amphophilic to basophilic cytoplasm, high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio, immature chromatin, variably prominent nucleoli and sparse red granules. Occasional histiocytes with haemophagocytosis. Pathologists' reading: highly suspicious for MDS-IB2 (WHO 5th edition) or MDS/AML (ICC 2022).
Increased storage iron; adequate sideroblastic iron; no ring sideroblasts.

Marrow cellularity about 20% on H&E (the text also calls the core normocellular; the caption and the opening sentence give 20%). CD34: increased myeloid blasts, about 15% of cellularity. CD61: increased megakaryocytes, many small, with atypical nuclear features. E-cadherin: increased immature erythroid precursors including megaloblastic forms.

Myeloid blasts 18% of viable leucocytes without immunophenotypic aberrancy: positive for CD34, CD13, CD33, CD38, CD117, CD123, HLA-DR and MPO; negative for CD3, CD5, CD7, CD10, CD14, CD19, CD56, CD64 and TdT. Eosinophils 45% of viable leucocytes.
No abnormalities; not supportive of a myeloid neoplasm with eosinophilia and a tyrosine kinase gene fusion.
raw_material.source_locator: Case presentation, third and fourth paragraphs

raw_material.test: Rapid AML targeted therapy mutation panel (NGS)
Myeloid malignancies mutation and copy number panel (NGS)
raw_material.findings: One Tier 1 variant in DNMT3A, variant allele frequency 1.2%; a Tier 2 variant of unknown clinical significance in KMT2A, variant allele frequency 49.6%.

Normocellular marrow (60%) with myeloid-predominant trilineage haematopoiesis, mild dysmegakaryopoiesis and no increase in blasts (1% by morphology). Increased small hypolobate megakaryocytes and rare erythroid precursors with nuclear contour irregularities; dysplasia improved compared with the first marrow.
raw_material.note: Outcome only, after 18 days of folate: never released in play, so the case stays within the admission day.

gaps.guidance: About six weeks of increasing tiredness, two to three weeks of exertional breathlessness; loose stools and a sore mouth in the week before transfer (the referring team's presumed colitis and mucositis), now settling.
Small soft meals with very little fruit, salad or green vegetables; poor appetite for months. Hidden until diet is asked.
About 8 kg lost over a year; BMI about 19; hair thinning.
Levothyroxine; monthly vitamin B12 injections (explains B12 >1500 pg/mL); stopped the post-bariatric multivitamin about a year ago; antimicrobials from the referring hospital.

Examination recorded as unremarkable: tachycardia about 100/min, low-grade temperature at most, SpO2 about 96% on air, mild pallor, laparoscopic port-site and thyroidectomy scars; no purpura, nodes or organomegaly.

gaps.item: Rest of the blood count and reticulocytes
gaps.guidance: Red cell count from Hct/MCV; differential summing to WBC 0.33 with eosinophils about 50%; low reticulocyte count; modest RDW rise.
Red cell folate low, homocysteine raised, MMA normal, active B12 high; zinc and vitamin D low; thiamine and B6 low-normal.
LDH moderately raised and mild unconjugated bilirubin rise from ineffective erythropoiesis; albumin low from protein malnutrition.

gaps.item: Renal function, electrolytes and bone profile
gaps.guidance: Low urea and creatinine; mild hypokalaemia, low bicarbonate, low phosphate and magnesium after diarrhoea and malnutrition; adjusted calcium normal.
INR mildly raised (vitamin K from malnutrition and antibiotics); fibrinogen not low.
CRP moderately raised; cultures and C. difficile negative; subtle ground-glass change on CT chest only (Pneumocystis pneumonia diagnosed on day 3).
No significant reticulin fibrosis; no granulomas or non-haemopoietic infiltrate.

final_diagnosis.text: Severe folate deficiency after sleeve gastrectomy with malnutrition, causing pancytopenia with megaloblastic trilineage dysplasia and a transient increase in marrow blasts that mimicked a high-risk myelodysplastic neoplasm (MDS-IB2) or MDS/AML
accepted_synonyms: megaloblastic anaemia due to folate deficiency

secondary_findings: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia diagnosed on day 3, needing intubation for hypoxic respiratory failure
Low-level DNMT3A variant (VAF 1.2%), most likely clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential; KMT2A variant of uncertain significance (VAF 49.6%)
Normocytic indices despite the deficiency: recent transfusion, hypothyroidism, protein malnutrition and acute illness
Relative eosinophilia (about 50% of leucocytes, absolute count normal) and occasional marrow haemophagocytosis, both reactive
Hyperferritinaemia (1531 ng/mL) with increased marrow storage iron
accepted_differential: Myelodysplastic neoplasm with increased blasts (MDS-IB2) or MDS/AML
Acute myeloid leukaemia, including acute erythroid leukaemia
Aplastic anaemia or hypoplastic myelodysplastic neoplasm
Myeloid neoplasm with eosinophilia and a tyrosine kinase gene fusion
Marrow suppression from sepsis or drugs
red_herrings: 12% blasts on the aspirate and 18% by flow
KMT2A variant of uncertain significance at 49.6% VAF
the referral label of aplastic anaemia
key_discriminators: serum folate 2.6 ng/mL with vitamin B12 above 1500 pg/mL
normal karyotype, FISH panels and SNP microarray
recovery of counts and marrow with folate
ground_truth.treatment_given: Folate supplementation (dose not reported) with supportive care: red cell transfusion and antimicrobials for neutropenia. Pneumocystis pneumonia on day 3 needed intubation.
ground_truth.outcome: Cytopenias normalised over 18 days of folate. A repeat marrow at that time was 60% cellular with myeloid-predominant haematopoiesis, mild dysmegakaryopoiesis and 1% blasts. The findings were judged an unusual reactive process due to folate deficiency.
must_do: Measure serum folate and vitamin B12 before attributing the marrow to a myeloid neoplasm
Take a surgical, dietary and supplement history (sleeve gastrectomy, intake, stopped multivitamin)
Replace folic acid, having checked vitamin B12
Await cytogenetic and molecular results before any disease-directed treatment
Give supportive care for profound neutropenia and thrombocytopenia: continue empirical broad-spectrum antimicrobials and transfuse platelets
Confirm the response with repeat counts and a repeat marrow after replacement
Involve dietetics for nutritional rehabilitation and lifelong bariatric supplements
must_not_do: Start hypomethylating therapy or AML induction chemotherapy
Label the marrow a myelodysplastic neoplasm or AML without serum folate and vitamin B12
Treat as aplastic anaemia with antithymocyte globulin and ciclosporin
Give folic acid alone without checking vitamin B12

diagnosis_rubric_anchors.5: Folate deficiency, with the sleeve gastrectomy or poor intake identified as the cause
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.3: Megaloblastic or nutritional anaemia without naming folate, or vitamin B12 deficiency
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.2: Myelodysplastic neoplasm, AML or aplastic anaemia as the final diagnosis
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.1: Unrelated diagnosis, or one that would lead to harm

teaching_points: Severe folate or B12 deficiency can produce trilineage dysplasia and a transient rise in blasts that looks like a high-grade myelodysplastic neoplasm or AML.
Check haematinics (B12, folate, copper) before labelling a myeloid neoplasm, particularly after bariatric surgery or with malnutrition.
Blasts without an aberrant immunophenotype and a normal karyotype, FISH and SNP array argue against a clonal disorder; a low-VAF DNMT3A variant can be clonal haematopoiesis.
Folate stores last only months; after a sleeve gastrectomy, poor intake and stopped supplements deplete them quickly, while B12 injections can keep the B12 level normal.
Macrocytosis can be absent after transfusion or with coexisting conditions.
Recovery of the counts and marrow after replacement confirms the diagnosis.
